narrative.morphology: One of the larger flagellated species of Lake Kinneret (after the dinoflagellates), and the only one with four flagella (Plate 1). It is heart-shaped (=cordiform, as its name) or cherry-shaped, ellipsoidal or almost spherical, never twisted, with four equal-length flagella emerging out of a pit or depression in the upper side of the cell (Plate 1). It has a red eyespot or stigma, and a single cup-shaped chloroplast usually with a basal pyrenoid. Two contractile vacuoles are present near the base of the flagella.
narrative.ecology:
Tetraselmis cordiformis usually occurs in the Kinneret plankton in small numbers of < 50 cells/mL (Fig. 1) and biomass not more than 4 g m⁻² (not shown). It is more abundant between February and April and again from August till November but absent in July and rare in December and January (Fig. 2). A technician-effect is noted in our data: a technician was replaced on 1 Jan 2013. It is evident in Fig. 1 that the newer technician counted this species more frequently than the previous one.
On a single unusual occasion in February 1996 Tetraselmis cordiformis formed an intense bloom that colored the entire lake with a strong grass-green color. This intense bloom disappeared within a few days and was missed by our weekly sampling, but photographic records remain (Plate 2). On another occasion, a massive bloom of this flagellated alga took place in a series of experimental tanks behind the Kinneret Limnological Institute. Again, the bloom was short lived and disappeared within days.
A distinct annual cycle of cell size is evident from our data: cells are smaller size in summer, larger in winter (Figs. 2, 3A). Cell size correlates well with water temperature (R²=0.48, Fig. 3B).
narrative.environmental_conditions: T. cordiformis occurred at the full range of water temperatures occurring in the lake, at conductivities > 1000 μS cm⁻¹ and Chloride > 210 mg L⁻¹, when Secchi transparency was 2-4 m, euphotic zone depth > 5 m, mostly at pH between 8–9, Chlorophyll < 400 mg m⁻², at alkalinities > 100 mg L⁻¹, when NH₄ was low but NO₃, Norg and DON were moderate (Fig. 4).
